title: 1952 H-bomb test as a signal to the cosmos
summary: Eric Weinstein tells of 1952 H-bomb test as a signal to the cosmos, about 1952 at Pacific, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: the concern that i have is that in 1952 what if there was someone there to hear what we said in the pacific if there was something or someone there to hear us they probably heard us as saying we're on the verge of being able to come visit
I think in 1952 we sent a signal to the cosmos which is that we're very very close to being in possession of root level knowledge
tellings.difference: Relayed second hand by Jesse Michels, and framed as a signal that we were close to 'root level knowledge' rather than close to being able to visit.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell Eric Weinstein's theory that the 1952 Pacific H-bomb test acted as a signal to whoever might be listening in the cosmos.

as_told.title: Weinstein: 1952 H-bomb sent a signal to the cosmos

plain: A mathematician and podcaster, Eric Weinstein, wonders what it meant when the United States set off a hydrogen bomb in the Pacific in 1952. He says that if something or someone was out there listening, they likely heard us saying we were close to being able to come visit them. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, later repeats the idea, framing it instead as a signal that we were close to deep, root-level knowledge of physics. If true, it would offer a reason why visitors might have started watching us.
